title: CDC's baby tips include copying the baby's sounds
summary: CDC's 2-month tips say to copy a baby's sounds and notice how long the baby keeps answering.
body: The 2-month activities page tells caregivers to copy the baby's sounds and see how long the baby keeps the exchange going by making sounds back. A nearby tip says to act excited, smile, and talk when the baby makes sounds, because that teaches turn-taking in a back-and-forth 'conversation.' These are printed suggestions for play, not milestones with an age and a percent. They are not instructions for one particular baby, and the page still says the materials are not a screening tool.

sources.title: Learn the Signs. Act Early. milestone page

sources.note: Supports the tips to copy the baby's sounds and to answer sounds so the baby practices back-and-forth turns. US federal page, public domain. Paraphrased, not quoted.
